analysis.title: AI Exposure in Insurance Portfolios – Just the Start
key_insights: Barclays sizes life insurers' digital infrastructure exposure at about 1.4% of bond portfolios across its peer set. That equals roughly 24% of statutory surplus as of 2Q26, falling to about 15% after an estimated adjustment for funds withheld assets.

Credit quality of the exposure is strong: 99% of the digital infrastructure exposure analyzed is investment grade and 68% is NAIC Class 1 (effectively A- or better). The ABS deals reviewed generally have LTVs of 40-60%.

On the funds-withheld-adjusted measure relative to surplus, FG (39%), CRBG (33%) and Athene (28%) screen highest versus a peer average of roughly 15%. Strong purchasing in 1Q26 and 2Q26 suggests allocations are rising quickly.

Barclays is comfortable with current balance-sheet risk but says total exposure is likely understated. The analysis does not fully capture digital infrastructure held through commercial mortgage loans or limited partnership/alternative investments.

If hyperscaler credit deteriorated significantly, Barclays argues the larger concern for life insurers would be broader recessionary fixed-income stress, not direct digital infrastructure exposure. It points readers to its prior recessionary and 2000-2002-style credit stress work.

At about 1.5% of the life sector's total investment portfolio (~$75bn of ~$6.0trn), AI-related securities are not a concentration risk even on a broad definition. Hyperscalers and data-center-backed corporate bonds are about 4.5% of the IG market versus about 3.5% of the life industry's bond portfolio, so insurers are underweight relative to the credit market.

Life insurers owned about 15% of the public/144A data center credit universe outstanding as of June 30. Moody's said US life insurers could add $50-100bn of AI ecosystem holdings by YE27 from an estimated $85bn at 2Q26, which Barclays calls quite plausible.
In some AI-related deals, US insurers own almost the entire transaction. Financing structures are evolving to fit insurer investment parameters, so concentrated positions could continue.

Insurers' risk tolerance for AI investments is unclear. A CoreWeave co-founder said 'unlimited' insurance capital is available to fund AI build-out, and Blackstone (insurance AUM $300bn+) said its insurance clients are 'mindful' of AI exposure but see room to expand capacity.

Risk varies by structure: corporate bond data center financing funds construction and front-loads risk, while ABS/CMBS finance stabilized assets with higher leverage and no amortization, creating refinancing and re-leasing risk at maturity. Barclays sees less fundamental risk in IG corporate bond data center exposure than in securitized credit.

NVDA and AVGO have collectively indicated close to $1tn of chip-related financing is expected over the next few years. Barclays expects insurers to participate meaningfully, and the depreciation curve of chips is uncertain, which adds residual collateral risk.

AI ecosystem IG bonds have seen spreads widen about 20bp this month. Barclays says life insurers are well placed to handle mark-to-market given regulatory capitalization and liquidity, but some holdings may be under-priced relative to where new issues are clearing.

The AI ecosystem is about $680bn of IG market value, roughly 7.5% of the index. Hyperscalers are $379bn (55%), semis $178bn (26%), hardware $86bn (13%), data centers $27bn (4%) and semicap $13bn (2%).

Moody's published a report on 21 October 2026 on life insurers' AI exposure, citing rapid allocation growth, correlation potential and indirect exposures. Smaller rating agencies also rate much of the data center ABS/CMBS: DBRS 36%, S&P 29%, KBRA 22%, Moody's and Fitch 13% each.

Yield is the draw for insurers. A-rated data center investments held by US life insurers had a weighted average book yield of 5.5% at 2Q26, about 100bp above the 4.6% book yield on all A-rated debt. Blackstone says it originates data-center and hard-asset debt at a 150bp premium to comparably-rated public credit.

market_movers.rationale: Barclays credit rates Broadcom bonds Market Weight, saying upgrades are likely priced in and positive catalysts are lacking. Chip financing could become a larger overhang, though bonds already reflect it to a degree.

sector_views.rationale: Barclays is comfortable with current AI-related exposure and sees low overall risk because allocations are small, but expects them to grow and says exposure warrants monitoring.

risk_factors: Total insurer exposure is likely understated because commercial mortgage loan and limited partnership/alternative holdings are not fully captured.
Concentrated insurer ownership of some AI-related deals could raise portfolio correlation.
Uncertain depreciation curve for chips weakens collateral backing for chip financings.
Refinancing and re-leasing risk on data center ABS/CMBS at maturity, given higher starting leverage and no amortization.
Insurers may hold AI exposure under-priced relative to new-issue clearing levels.
Rating agency scrutiny and reliance on smaller rating agencies with shorter track records.
A significant deterioration in hyperscaler credit would likely matter more through broader recessionary fixed-income stress.
charts_described: Figure 15 plots the basis differential vs the IG index in bp for IG ex AI ecosystem, the AI ecosystem and the AI ecosystem ex hyperscalers, Oct-25 to Oct-26, with the AI ecosystem widening versus the index, led by hyperscalers.
Figure 16 shows the AI ecosystem at about $680bn of IG market value: hyperscalers $379bn (55%), semis $178bn (26%), hardware $86bn (13%), data centers $27bn (4%), semicap $13bn (2%).
Figure 10 table: average digital infrastructure exposure to surplus is 23.5% including funds withheld and 15.3% excluding them. Athene is 105.3% including and 28.4% excluding funds withheld.
Figure 17 shows DC ABS tranche ratings by share outstanding: A 76%, AAA 13%, BBB 8%, AA 2%, BB 1%. Figure 18 shows DC CMBS: AAA 55%, BBB 14%, A 12%, AA 10%, BB 6%, B 2%, NR 1%.
vol_and_positioning: The AI ecosystem IG bond cohort has widened about 20bp versus the index this month, led by hyperscalers.
Spread volatility may persist as the credit market absorbs rising supply from AI ecosystem issuers.
cross_bank_references: Moody's has said US life insurers could reasonably increase AI ecosystem holdings by $50-$100bn by YE27, from its 2Q26 estimate of $85bn.

tension_points.bull_case: Exposure is about 1.4% of bonds, 99% investment grade, 68% NAIC 1, with ABS LTVs of 40-60%. Insurers are underweight AI/data center credit versus the IG market (about 3.5% vs 4.5%) and earn about 100bp more book yield on A-rated data center paper.
tension_points.bear_case: Exposure is growing fast and is likely understated. Insurers own nearly entire transactions in some deals, risk tolerances are unclear, chip collateral depreciation is uncertain, and AI bonds may be under-priced versus new-issue levels.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Significant deterioration in hyperscaler credit, which Barclays says would matter mainly through broader recessionary fixed-income stress.

theme_stances.key_argument: Current exposure is manageable because allocations are small and high quality, but it is growing and warrants monitoring.
theme_stances.evidence: we are comfortable with the risk currently on life insurer balance sheets

theme_stances.key_argument: Spread volatility may persist as the market digests rising AI issuer supply, and some insurer holdings may be under-priced relative to new-issue levels.
theme_stances.evidence: spread volatility may persist as the credit market digests increasing supply
